{"id":190772,"tenderTitle":"DUAL SATELLITE IN-ORBIT TESTBED FOR SENSING AND COMMUNICATION FOR LOW-POWER DEVICES (ARTES AT 3E.034)","tenderNumber":"1-13607","tenderDescription":"Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and launch a dual satellite in-orbit testbed for sensing and communication for low-power devices with both transmit and receive user capability and inter-satellite link.Targeted Improvements: Enabling the development of protocols and operations concepts for the communication and geolocation from space with low-power terrestrial devices.Description: There is currently no European in-orbit capability to test and validate low-power communication directlybetween LEO satellites and standard ground devices. This limits the development of protocols, modulation schemes, and system architectures for emerging applications in low-power geolocation, environmental sensing, and ubiquitous IoT connectivity. This activity will develop a test bed that supports the exploration of disruptive use cases in low power direct communications between terrestrialdevices and LEO satellites. The testbed will comprise two satellites operating in tandem that can (at a minimum):- Establish a bi-directional low power (Tx/Rx) communications link between satellite and terrestrial devices- Provide Inter-satellite links (ISL) between the two, supporting cross-traffic, redundancy as well as geolocation of devices and interference sources- Test new protocols (e.g. SigFox, LoraWan, Bluetooth) and modulation schemes optimised for low-power signals.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 with a budget of up to 3MEuro will design and develop a dual-satellite payload testbed able to directly communicate with terrestrial low-power devices. It will mature the key technologies and communication protocols from using simulation and laboratory testing to demonstrate feasibility and system readiness for in-orbit demonstration. Deliverables from Phase 1 are a summary report and full engineering model.- Phase 2 will build the flight equipment, launch, and operate the dual-satellite platform toexperiment with direct low-power, low frequency communications in orbit. The in-orbit experiment will test real-time user communications, validate geolocation concepts, evaluate inter-satellite link performance and collect performance data to inform future protocol standardisation and system architectures.
